summary: Iteration 5 verified the two new deliverables end-to-end. Backend (13/13 pytest pass in ~4s, new file /app/backend/tests/test_iter5_cadence_otp.py): (1) Autopilot cadence config — GET /api/autopilot/config as admin returns is_admin=true, cap (default 10), daily_proposals (default 3), autopilot bool. POST /api/autopilot/config {cap:6} updates cap; cap is clamped to [1,50] (cap:999 -> 50, cap:0 -> 1). POST {daily_proposals:4} sets it to 4, and POST {daily_proposals:20} with cap=6 clamps down to 6. POST /api/proposals/generate with cap=5/daily_proposals=2 returned count in [1..2] (real Groq, respects the clamp). (2) OTP wiring — POST /api/auth/otp/request {identifier:'admin@marketing.ai'} returns 200 channel='email' sent_to=admin@marketing.ai (real SMTP send, no dev_otp leaked); subsequent /api/auth/otp/verify with code '000000' returns 401. POST /api/auth/otp/request {identifier:'+919121664855'} returns 200 channel='sms' with masked sent_to starting '+91' and ending '55' with bullet mask, no dev_otp leaked (real Twilio Verify start executed — SMS was sent to the admin phone as expected). /api/auth/otp/verify with wrong code '000000' returns 401 'Invalid or expired code' (real Twilio VerificationCheck rejected). Unknown email and unknown phone both return 404. Frontend (real browser, admin login): /approvals page renders cadence-stepper (value/inc/dec) and cap-stepper (admin only). Setting cap to 6 via cap-inc/dec works, cadence-inc from 3->4 shows sonner toast 'Autopilot will propose 4 campaigns per day', clicking + past the cap clamps cadence at 6 (never exceeds cap), cadence-dec from 6->5 works, and both values persist across full page reload (cadence=6, cap=6 after reload). Screenshot saved at /app/test_reports/approvals_cadence.png.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py set_autopilot_config (line 1104): non-admin owners passing 'cap' silently trigger _require_admin -> 403; that's correct, but if both cap and daily_proposals are sent by a non-admin, the daily_proposals write is aborted with the same 403. Consider ignoring cap for non-admin instead of failing the whole request, so owners can save cadence in a single call.

server.py _get_autopilot_cap: no upper-bound check on the stored value. If a stored settings doc has cap=1000 (e.g. manual DB edit), reads return 1000. Consider min(50, max(1, int(value))) in the getter to defend against drift.

server.py generate_proposals uses profile.get('daily_proposals', 3) — if the AI (Groq) returns fewer proposals than requested (JSON drift), the response 'count' can be lower than daily_proposals. Not a bug (count is truthful), but the frontend toast currently reports 'X proposal(s) generated' from the server so no mismatch — worth noting for observability.

auth.py otp_request (phone branch, line 182): failure paths raise 502/503, but if Twilio's start returns ok=False with an empty detail (rate-limited), the caller only sees 'Could not send SMS code:'. Consider surfacing Twilio's REST error 'code' field for support.

auth.py otp_verify (line 254) deletes the OTP record on the first successful verify — good. But on wrong code it does NOT increment a fail counter or expire after N attempts. Add a per-user attempt counter (max 5) to prevent brute force on the email 6-digit code (Twilio side already rate-limits SMS).

Frontend Approvals.jsx setCadence optimistically updates state then calls the API; if the API fails, load() is called on error — good. But between the optimistic bump and the API response, a user rapidly clicking + can send multiple overlapping POSTs. Consider debouncing or disabling the button while in-flight.

rca of the issue: No blocking issues. Autopilot config is enforced correctly server-side: admin-only cap writes (403 for non-admin), cap clamped to [1,50], daily_proposals clamped to [1, cap] on both write (POST) and read (GET), and /api/proposals/generate uses the same clamped per_day. OTP correctly branches on identifier type (email vs phone), real SMTP for email and real Twilio Verify (start + check) for phone, with no dev_otp leaked in production paths, 401 on wrong code, and 404 on unknown identifier.
